attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: There is no valid operation converting an arbitrary global H circuit into local SAT-range separators without either neutralizing the generator or using a new real-SAT, nonrelativizing locality principle.
steps: Assume a circuit A of size S<N^{1+epsilon} decides H_N^G.
Use A to define a residual positive distribution over generated bags and try to build one-sided local predicates accepting at least one satisfiable query per positive bag.
Attempt SAT self-reduction on a generated formula y=G_N(x,j); this manipulates assignments inside y but does not produce nearby inputs x' that alter only y.
Add a hypothetical neutralizing map E_j(y); then A(E_j(y)) exactly decides SAT on R_j, giving extraction but also demagnifying the source obligation to restricted SAT hardness.
Therefore the useful bridge is not separator hardness alone but the quantitative nonrelativizing extraction bound D<=S/N^{1+sigma}+N^kappa with kappa<epsilon-sigma.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The threshold lemma is conditional; the needed extraction theorem is unproved, and the neutralizing implementation collapses the intended weak-source character of the route.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: locality extraction threshold

assumptions: The separator lower bound is proved for the actual generated range, not for an enlarged promise range.

The proof is nonrelativizing; planted-control oracle worlds are admitted as a falsifier for relativizing versions.
Polylogarithmic query length keeps SAT substitution cost N^{q+o(1)} for every fixed polynomial SAT exponent.
definitions: source object: H_N^G(x)=OR_{1<=j<=N^q} SAT(G_N(x,j)), where x has length N, each query has length L=(log N)^d with d>1, and C(G_N)<=N^rho.

controlled interface: arbitrary circuit for H_N is transformed into a one-sided local separator cover for the actual generated SAT bags, with denominator D_{sigma,E} and error budget E.

target-preserving condition: max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, extraction loss kappa<epsilon-sigma, error E<N^{epsilon-o(1)}, and the extraction must use real SAT semantics rather than relativizing oracle access.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: There is no valid low-tail compiler for P or unrestricted SIZE, and Fourier tail is not stable under NP-complete recodings with easy high-frequency branches.
steps: Assume a proposed route proves W_{>t}(SAT_m)>epsilon for t=polylog(m).
Apply LMN: if t exceeds C_d(k log m+log(1/epsilon))^{d-1}, then SAT_m is not in AC0_d[m^k].
Try to upgrade to SAT_m notin P by asserting that P or SIZE(m^k) computations have low Fourier tail at comparable t.
Test the assertion on PARITY_m, which is in P and linear-size circuits but has all Fourier mass at degree m.
Test encoding robustness on the branched language L_{n,r,p}, which is NP-complete yet has constant tail mass coming solely from an easy parity slice.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves at most an AC0 lower bound under a quantitative LMN threshold; it supplies no route-level evidence for P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier audit for Fourier-tail lower-bound routes

assumptions: d and k are fixed constants; s=m^k is the AC0 size threshold.
Fourier degree is measured on the same m-bit representation used by the target circuits.
The lower-bound claim is about tail mass, not merely existence of one high-degree coefficient.
No advice-dependent encoding of the truth table is allowed unless it is counted in the target interface.
definitions: source object: the uniform truth table of f_m=SAT_m or a named NP carrier on m input bits, represented as a {-1,1}-valued function with Walsh-Fourier coefficients under the uniform cube.
target object: depth-d unbounded fan-in AC0 circuits of size at most m^k; the audited non-target is unrestricted Boolean SIZE(m^k) and uniform P machines.
controlled interface: the LMN concentration theorem, which upper-bounds the Fourier mass above degree t for every circuit in the named AC0 target class.

target-preserving condition: a P-vs-NP transfer would need a proof that every P-time or SIZE(m^k) decider for the same m-bit language has low Fourier tail at the same t and epsilon parameters, with no padding or encoding leakage.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: We still lack a no-advice E-uniform selector that proves robust bad-ball avoidance while having alpha_int at least epsilon. Known explicitness methods provide either local/block access and become easy, or only nonconstructive random existence.
steps: Start with the random robust low-D family from L49.3, which satisfies the MCSP no-side and sparse-correction requirements with overwhelming probability.
Try to derandomize it by a seed-indexed selector S_m(a) whose full output stream is E-time computable and whose image count is 2^{Dm+o(m)}.
Give S_m an indexed restart feature so the verifier or unranking algorithm can recompute a requested block of length 2^{lambda m} without scanning the whole row.
For a fixed seed a, hardwire a into the block decoder. On input x, compute the block index and offset, run the interval decoder, and select the desired bit.
This gives row circuits of size 2^{max(lambda,tau(lambda),chi(lambda))m+o(m)}. If this exponent is below epsilon, the selected row is not on the MCSP no-side.
Therefore PRG-like, locally decodable, or checkpoint-rich repairs cannot instantiate the random carrier unless their interval access exponent already meets the MCSP threshold.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a valid route-level obstruction and extraction audit, not a proof of P != NP. It only says which MCSP carrier sources would transfer and which are formally invalid.

branch_outputs.branch_title: MCSP / Meta-Complexity Carrier Transfer: interval-decoder leakage audit

assumptions: Rows are Boolean truth tables on m input bits; unrestricted circuit size is the MCSP measure.
For fixed row seed a, nonuniform circuits may hardwire a; row-seed length is not a hardness resource.

An interval decoder receives a row seed and a block index and returns all bits in that block, or equivalently has a restart mechanism whose advice/checkpoint can be computed with exponent chi(lambda).
The claimed MCSP threshold is s_m=2^{epsilon m} with constant epsilon>0, not epsilon(m)=o(1).
definitions: source object: a uniform low-distinct-image MCSP certificate carrier U_m of N=2^m bit truth tables, with row seed length at most Dm and claimed row hardness against unrestricted circuits of size 2^{epsilon m}.
target object: an E-uniform multiplexed language obtained by ranking the distinct carrier rows, intended to yield an E circuit lower bound with exponent delta below epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
controlled interface: sequential row emission is allowed, but any indexed block, interval, restart, or checkpoint decoder for row bits is charged by exponents lambda, tau(lambda), and chi(lambda).

target-preserving condition: the carrier remains no-advice, kappa-dense across source lengths, E-canonicalizable, and has no subthreshold interval decoder; otherwise the extracted E lower bound is invalid.

equations.label: row-size-from-interval-decoder
equations.valid_when: Valid when the interval decoder is indexed by block number and the fixed row seed may be hardwired nonuniformly into the final row circuit.

equations.label: interval-leakage-falsifier
equations.latex: inf_{0<=lambda<=1} max(lambda,tau(lambda),chi(lambda)) < epsilon => U_m is not an MCSP no-side carrier at threshold 2^{epsilon m}
equations.valid_when: Applies when the source soundness claims every accepted row has unrestricted circuit complexity exceeding the named MCSP threshold.

equations.label: admissible-source-cutoff
equations.latex: alpha_int(U)=inf_lambda max(lambda,tau(lambda),chi(lambda));  valid source requires epsilon <= alpha_int(U)+o(1)
equations.valid_when: Requires a declared access profile for the source emitter and excludes hidden advice that would change the checkpoint exponent.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A proposed carrier fails this lemma if a falsifier supplies any lambda with max(lambda,tau(lambda),chi(lambda))<epsilon; standard locally computable PRG selectors fail at lambda=0.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-specific falsifier theorem: it does not prove P != NP, but it rejects explicit carrier constructions whose sequential selector has subthreshold block restart or interval access.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Interval-access leakage lemma. Let U_m be a low-image MCSP carrier whose rows are N-bit truth tables, N=2^m, and suppose every accepted row is claimed to have circuit complexity greater than s_m=2^{epsilon m}. If there is an indexed interval decoder which, for some block exponent lambda, outputs the 2^{lambda m}-bit block of any row from its row seed and block index using circuit or restart complexity 2^{tau(lambda)m+o(m)} and checkpoint complexity 2^{chi(lambda)m+o(m)}, then every row has unrestricted circuits of size at most 2^{max{lambda,tau(lambda),chi(lambda)}m+o(m)}. Hence a valid no-side MCSP carrier must satisfy inf_lambda max{lambda,tau(lambda),chi(lambda)} >= epsilon, up to lower-order terms.

assumptions: Canonical distinct-image unranking runs within E time after including the rank overhead.
The hard row is actually present among accepted distinct images, either by universal soundness or by the existential multiplexing repair.
No nonuniform length selector is used to choose the hard source lengths.
definitions: N=2^m is the row truth-table length.
Distinct-image entropy D means the number of distinct rows is at most 2^{Dm+o(m)} after canonical quotienting.
kappa-density means every target input length n has a source length m with n <= kappa(1+D)m+o(m).
The multiplexed target stores the row rank and the row input as the target input.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Multiplexed extraction remains valid after the interval audit. If a kappa-dense sequence of carrier lengths has distinct-image entropy D, E-canonical unranking, and at least one accepted row of MCSP complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m} on each source length, then the certificate-index multiplexed language is in E and has circuit lower bound exponent any delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)). The new interval condition is source admissibility, not an additional loss in the extraction exponent.

assumptions: epsilon<1 and eta<1, so the union bound exponent is dominated by the truth-table length 2^m.
The circuit model is unrestricted Boolean circuits of fan-in two with standard encoding count 2^{O(s log s)}.
No claim is made that the random family is constructible without advice.
definitions: Bad balls are Hamming balls around truth tables computed by circuits of size at most 2^{epsilon m}.
Robust row hardness means distance greater than r from every subthreshold circuit truth table.
The random family is not an E-uniform carrier unless a selector and soundness certificate are supplied.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Random robust low-D carriers still exist combinatorially, but the existence proof is non-explicit and gives no valid source. For fixed constants D<1, epsilon<1, and correction radius r=2^{eta m} with eta<1, a uniformly random family of 2^{Dm} rows avoids all r-balls around circuits of size 2^{epsilon m} with overwhelming probability. This separates the combinatorial packing issue from the explicit selector issue.
